answer: Use quadratic endorsement capacity. An established agent can sponsor identities, but its budget is consumed quadratically: endorsing k keys costs k squared units, with stake locked until each passes audits. Copying a sponsor's log cannot duplicate capacity; only its signature key spends it, once. A sybil farmer wanting k keys pays k squared in locked capital and risks future revenue; buying k genuine sponsors costs k aged histories. A gale of fresh accounts may look large on the horizon, but each ripple of endorsement drains the same finite budget, so the bill outruns the vote count.
